```{python}
    (f"{c['pipe_length_km']} km", "of main"),
    (f"{c['sensors']}", "sensor nodes"),
    (f"{c['dmas']}", "district areas"),

for n, l in cells:
    print(f'<div><div class="n">{n}</div><div class="l">{l}</div></div>')
print('</div>')
```

A campus water network exists as five disconnected artefacts: 
1) a CAD drawing in the estate office
2) a hydraulic model on someone's laptop
3) a spreadsheet of sensor locations
4) a firmware repository, and 
5) a diagram of what the sensors measure

Each is intelligible on its own. None of them can answer a question
that spans two of them.

This project connects all five. The result is a graph in which *"which pH
sensors sit on dead ends where modelled pressure falls in the bottom fifth of
their district?"* is a single query rather than a week of cross-referencing.

## How it fits together

| Layer | Artefact | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Physical network | AC1015 AutoCAD drawing, 66 estate annotations | [Source data](01-source-data.qmd) |
| Hydraulic model | EPANET 2.2, Hazen-Williams, peak demand | [Hydraulic model](02-hydraulic-model.qmd) |
| Monitoring design | K-means districts + hierarchical overlay filter | [Sensor placement](03-sensor-placement.qmd) |
| Instrumentation | Five-parameter water-quality node | [IoT node](04-iot-node.qmd) |
| Semantics | OWL 2 DL, aligned to SOSA/SSN and QUDT | [Ontology](05-ontology.qmd) |
| Knowledge graph | 8,554 triples, schema derived from the data | [Knowledge graph](06-knowledge-graph.qmd) |
| Query | Client-side SPARQL over the whole graph | [Explorer](07-explorer.qmd) |

## The part that was actually hard

Not the ontology. The drawing.

The mains share a layer with the campus base map, the sheet carries two copies
of the network, the diameter annotations are in four different notations, and
the branch lines are drawn as separate polylines that stop short of the mains
they connect to — 51 disconnected islands with a median gap of 31 m. A naive
import produces something EPANET refuses to solve, and the failure mode is a
bare `Error 110` with no indication that the cause is topological.

Most of the engineering here is in getting from that drawing to a graph a
solver will accept, without silently deleting the parts that do not fit.

## Honest limits

::: {.caveat}
**The georeference is solved, not surveyed.** The CAD carries no CRS. The
transform comes from optimising the network footprint against a digitised
campus boundary — good to roughly 10–30 m, which is adequate for sampling a
30 m DEM and not adequate for anything else.

**Elevations are FABDEM at 30 m**, so nodes closer together than the posting
share a value.

**Pressures are modelled**, from a single steady-state run at a 2.5 peak factor,
and inherit every assumption above.

**48 island-bridging pipes are not in the drawing.** They are the shortest
connectors that make the network solvable, and they are reported on every run.
:::
